transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So the surface boy crawled back down. I thought the darkness frightened you enough the first time to keep your feet on the grass above.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not afraid of the dark anymore.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is the first lie of your return, and you say it with a straight face. I can hear your heart hammering like a trapped bird. Why did you come back?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I remembered something about the well you need to know.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Need is a bold word to bring to someone older than your bloodline. Last time you arrived with tears and apologies. What knowledge have you suddenly acquired?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know why the black river is rising.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The river rises because it chooses to rise, not because of some secret tucked in your pocket. Still, I am listening. You rehearsed this, didn't you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's rising because the seal at the top is broken.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A broken seal. Dramatic—like a story old women tell to keep children obedient. You are trying much harder to be interesting this time.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My grandfather has the other half of the stone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Now you connect the water below to the stones above. Better work than begging. Does this stone have a name?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's called the Eye of the Mountain.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The Eye of the Mountain—like something men hum when they're too old to speak clearly. If it is so important, why isn't it in your hand right now?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My grandfather said it can't enter until the path is clear.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Your grandfather has a rule for every inconvenience. Convenient, too, that it explains why you arrived empty-handed. Tell me—what happens if this stone stays on the surface?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The river will rise until it swallows the gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Swallows the gate. I have watched that river for centuries and it has never hungered for my door. You give the water teeth it does not possess, though I admire the effort.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's hungry because the seal is broken.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You cling to your story like a mule with a loaded cart. Last time you faltered when I pressed you; today you dig your heels in. Do you truly believe I do not know the tides of my own home?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You've been inside too long to see the change.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Insolence wrapped as concern. You have grown a taller spine since we last spoke, even if your legs still shake. Suppose I indulge you—what does Omar have to do with this stone?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's the only one who can hold it safely.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The boy who insulted the Well is the only vessel for its salvation. That is the most convenient piece of your entire tale. You want me to believe fate chose him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It chose our family long ago.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Your family was chosen, and yet at the rim he did not speak binding words. He screamed insults like a bored child kicking stones. How does your grand destiny account for that stupidity?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He didn't know the truth. Only I did.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So the secret was entrusted to the trembling brother, while the 'chosen vessel' remained ignorant enough to be snatched by the very thing he provoked. The architecture is collapsing. It does not hold weight.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I kept it from him to keep him safe from the burden.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You kept him safe by daring him to insult the power you claim to understand? You hear the cracks, don't you. You cannot reconcile the boy who made a foolish dare with the guardian of an ancient seal.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I made a mistake that day, but the stone is real.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: As real as your sudden confidence. A prop you built because you feared returning empty-handed. There is no seal, little liar, and the river rises on the slow tides of time.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I needed something you would want.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You thought I was a merchant, trading passage for trinkets and secrets. Clever—better than sobbing—but it is still a costume, and it has slipped.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I had to try something new.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You did try, and for a moment you almost believed yourself. Now the stage is bare, and you are only a boy again. Why are you still standing there?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because I can't leave him here alone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is—the tapestry burns away and leaves ash. You came back to a place of nightmares, knowing exactly what I am, because you could not walk away.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm the older brother. I'm supposed to look out for him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Duty is a heavy chain, and fear usually snaps it clean. You were safe on the surface, free to let time do its work, yet you crawled back down on purpose.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't sleep up there knowing he's down here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you chose the terror of the pit over the quiet torture of your own thoughts. Trading a slow poison for a quick death—an oddly honest bargain.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's not a bargain. It's my brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak that word like it should command the world. You have no plan, no stone, no leverage—only a child's need to undo what is already done.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't need a plan to know I belong with him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You belong where the sun shines and the air does not taste of oil. Most who flee my father's realm run until their lungs burn and never look back. You turned around.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I couldn't run from this.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You came back with nothing but guilt, knowing I might snap you in two, and you are still standing there waiting. You are a very foolish boy.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not leaving without Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You lied to my face twice, yet you do not retreat when the lie collapses. I expected you to run the moment your story crumbled, but you stay rooted like a stubborn weed. It is irritating—and oddly compelling.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's my responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fear usually tastes sour, but yours has changed. It tastes like resolve. You are terrified of me, but more terrified of returning to that empty room above without him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know what that means. I just need to pass.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You built a false key because you assumed I required payment in wonders. But you yourself are the curiosity. A thousand warriors would have fled—yet the lying boy came back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm just a boy from the village.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are a boy who walked back into the mouth of a beast because he left a piece of himself behind. My father hoards the memories of the lost, but I guard the threshold—and I find I am tired of blocking your path.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's my brother, not a piece of me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The distinction means nothing to the darkness, but it clearly means everything to you. The gears behind me are old; the sound will be ugly when the way unbars itself. Do not flinch, little liar.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The doors are actually moving.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not thank me. You are walking into a deeper throat than mine, and my father is not amused by loyalty. Go find your thief before I remember why I enjoy keeping my treasures.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm coming for you, Omar.
